title: Short chain fatty acids in human large intestine, portal, hepatic and venous blood
authors: Cummings JH, Pomare EW, Branch WJ, Naylor CP, Macfarlane GT
population: Six sudden-death victims sampled at autopsy within four hours of death
funder: not stated for the study; the acknowledgements state that E.W. Pomare was supported by the University of Otago, The Royal Australian College of Physicians and the Todd Foundation, New Zealand. Author affiliation: MRC Dunn Clinical Nutrition Centre and Department of Histopathology, Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge.
result: Total short-chain fatty acids were 13 ± 6 mmol/kg in the terminal ileum and 131 ± 9 mmol/kg in the caecum. Molar ratios of acetate:propionate:butyrate in colonic contents were 57:22:21; butyrate fell to 8% of the three in portal blood, and propionate fell from 21% to 12% between portal and hepatic venous blood. Total SCFA in blood were 375 ± 70 (portal), 148 ± 42 (hepatic) and 79 ± 22 (peripheral) µmol/L. The authors interpret the fall in butyrate as greater uptake by the colonic epithelium.
